description: A CPS-split `bump()` whose server batch is NON-monotone (`set n = n + 1` reads the column it assigns, so re-running it advances the counter again) under `idempotency-store="none"`. Per §19.9.6 there is no key storage for the retry envelope, so E-CPS-NONIDEM-NO-STORAGE fires (§34: Error). The client/server INTERLEAVE is load-bearing: route-inference only builds a `cpsSplit` for a body containing a reactive assignment, so a wholly-server function is never CPS-eligible and this code cannot fire on one.
rationale: §19.9.6 — a CPS body-split turns one function into SEVERAL server requests, so any batch that is not monotone can be applied twice by a retry. scrml's answer is a Stripe-style idempotency key, which needs somewhere to live. With `idempotency-store="none"` there is nowhere, so the compiler refuses at compile time rather than shipping a double-charge that only appears under a retry — the §49 no-silent-bad-output posture. The three escapes it names are all real: match the `db=` driver, import `scrml:redis`, or assert `.idempotent()` if the batch is monotone-by-construction.
